title: Chicken parmesan
equipment: Rimmed sheet pan with a wire rack

items: 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ lb), halved horizontally into 4 cutlets about ½ inch thick
1 large egg, beaten with 1 Tbsp water
½ cup vegetable oil, for frying
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)

steps: Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Set a wire rack in a rimmed sheet pan. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.
Pat the cutlets dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper. Set up 3 shallow dishes: the flour, the beaten egg, and the breadcrumbs mixed with ¼ cup parmesan.
Coat each cutlet in flour and shake off the extra, dip it in egg and let it drip, then press it into the breadcrumbs on both sides.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until a pinch of breadcrumbs sizzles right away. Fry 2 cutlets at a time 3–4 min per side, until deep golden and they read 165°F in the thickest part. Move them to the wire rack.
While the chicken fries, cook the spaghetti until al dente. Drain and toss with 2 cups of the warm marinara.
Spoon about ¼ cup of the remaining marinara over each cutlet and top with the mozzarella. Broil 2–4 min, until the cheese is melted and browned in spots. Watch closely.
Serve the chicken over the spaghetti, sprinkled with parmesan.
tips: Air fryer: spray the breaded cutlets with oil and cook at 400°F for 10–12 min, flipping halfway, until 165°F. Add the sauce and cheese and cook 1–2 min more to melt.
Let the breaded cutlets sit 10 min before frying so the coating sticks better.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the cutlets on a sheet pan in a 375°F oven 12–15 min, until they reach 165°F; the microwave makes the breading soggy. Freeze breaded, uncooked cutlets up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge before frying.
